premise: A lithified burrow cast appears to hold two ancient animals; the reveal reframes them from enemies to unlikely shelter-mates, while clearly marking behavioral interpretation as inference.

claimsSupported: The script explicitly frames behavioral interpretation as likely/inference/most plausible interpretation.
The visual treatment is planned as 3D illustrative reconstruction/X-ray animation, not real footage.
The twist beat is framed around absence of bite marks as a clue, not a definitive hunt claim.
claimsNotSupported: No primary-source citations are attached in this package yet; taxa identity, injury diagnosis, and burial mechanism must be verified against Stage 1/primary literature before publish.
The exact species pairing, aestivation state, and flood-cause sequence are not presented as confirmed observed fact.

narration: This rock holds two animals. Two hundred fifty million years ago, one curled up asleep. It was a mammal relative, beside an amphibian. Wait. They were not enemies. The amphibian's ribs were healing, with no bite marks. So this was not a hunt. The likely story: it crawled in for shelter. The other was probably in aestivation, a deep dormancy. Then a flood filled the burrow and sealed them. That is the clue the rock kept. This rock holds two animals.
screenDescription: 9:16 vertical cinematic 3D short. Macro lithified burrow cast, synchrotron-style X-ray sweep, sagittal cutaways of curled mammal-relative and injured amphibian skeletons, Vertigo dolly-zoom twist, checklist overlay, inference-labeled ghosted shelter entry, split-panel aestivation diagram, 0.25x slow-motion sediment flood, and seamless loop back to the opening X-ray sweep. All visuals are illustrative reconstructions.
